There are 20 open PRs: 10 look clean or advisory-only, and 10 need additional changes. I made no code changes and submitted no GitHub reviews or approvals.

Most standard CI jobs are green across Linux, macOS, and Windows. The red “Entire Gates” checks are usually missing human approval rather than test failures. PR #136’s latest Windows test and gate were still running at the final snapshot.

## PR walkthrough

1. **[#97 — Experimental SCIP snapshot export](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/97) — changes needed.**  
   Adds binary `snapshot --format scip`, deterministic SCIP symbols/occurrences, and a JSON omission note on stderr. Two blockers remain: the omission note retains only warning/failure counts and discards their machine-readable codes, paths, and details ([root.go](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/831657e1027854418428295ecc614821113ba9e4/internal/cli/root.go#L419-L431)); and Windows project roots are encoded incorrectly as file URIs ([compact_snapshot.go](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/831657e1027854418428295ecc614821113ba9e4/internal/sem/compact_snapshot.go#L732-L736)). The draft is also 53 commits behind and conflicts in `README.md`, `docs/DETAILS.md`, and the renamed semantic-provider requirements document. Its green CI predates current `main`.

2. **[#126 — Escape fatal stderr errors](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/126) — clean.**  
   Routes fatal error text through `termsafe.Line`, preventing repository-controlled ESC, C1, or newline bytes from manipulating terminal output. It deliberately leaves the progress bar’s own control sequences intact. The subprocess-based entry-point test and all platform CI pass.

3. **[#127 — Guard cache-key ignore reads](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/127) — clean.**  
   Replaces bare ignore-file reads with regular-file checks, descriptor-level verification, and nonblocking FIFO opens. Symlinks to legitimate regular ignore files remain supported and preserve existing cache keys. Tests cover devices, FIFOs, races, and large legal ignore files.

4. **[#128 — Protect `cat-file --batch` requests](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/128) — changes needed.**  
   Correctly rejects newline and trailing-CR paths before they desynchronize Git’s line protocol, resolves newline-bearing revisions, and gives nonbatchable paths bounded argv-based readers. A reproduced edge remains: [`ShowFileDigested`](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/503a8d1361b07dc1ea0fc5b8f10d391f585b5e41/internal/gitutil/git.go#L675-L687) obtains size without checking object type. An oversized gitlink is treated as a blob, then `git cat-file blob` fails; the dependents path can abort analysis. The size probe needs to be type-aware.

5. **[#129 — Exclude credential stores](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/129) — clean.**  
   Adds case-insensitive built-in path exclusions for dotenv files, private keys, credential files, and data/config files under secrets directories. The rules cover worktree, committed-tree, graph, search, needle-grep, and persistent-cache paths, while an explicit include file remains the deliberate override. Its limitation—path classification rather than secret-content scanning—is documented.

6. **[#130 — Bound ignore-file memory](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/130) — minor changes needed.**  
   Adds 1 MiB per-file, 4,096-rule per-matcher, and 65,536 retained-rule listing limits. The committed vendor-rule matcher currently receives a separate budget from the explicit/`.graphignore` matcher, allowing roughly twice the documented aggregate limit ([provider.go](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/5abeded3e066da1bddadc9eb056601bdc923d9b4/internal/sem/provider.go#L9767-L9778)). It should share the listing budget.

7. **[#131 — Protect graph-bench fetch refs](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/131) — changes needed.**  
   Validates manifest refs, uses end-of-options where supported, handles SHA-256 IDs, and verifies lock-object checkouts. One warm-cache ambiguity remains: a raw hex-shaped manifest ref can resolve to a stale same-named local branch rather than the fetched object ([main.go](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/b6057c65715c96a30caf76233a37290f5a7be9d1/cmd/graph-bench/main.go#L560-L570)). Peel it to a commit and verify `HEAD`, as the lock path already does.

8. **[#132 — Never index Git administrative directories](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/132) — changes needed.**  
   Adds comprehensive detection of `.git`, linked/separate Git dirs, gitfiles, commondirs, structural Git dirs, and hidden pointer targets. The latest head removes all pruning while searching excluded trees, but that creates an unbudgeted, non-cancellable recursive scan of potentially millions of ignored directories ([provider.go](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/3c1353dde59ca0f635618b826e50d6f1f7d9b934/internal/sem/provider.go#L11071-L11114)). Other issues: one unreadable directory globally promotes unrelated Git-shaped fixtures; an oversized `.git` file with an early NUL is accepted although Git rejects it; and tests inherit interactive editor settings. The branch is also three commits behind `main`.

9. **[#133 — Validate diff revisions](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/133) — clean.**  
   Rejects empty, NUL-containing, and leading-dash revisions before they enter Git argv, closing option injection through `commit`, `diff`, and `analyze`. Ordinary hashes, branches, and revision expressions remain accepted. Tests and CI pass.

10. **[#134 — Harden Git subprocess configuration](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/134) — clean.**  
    Centralizes Git process creation and disables repository-controlled fsmonitor/signature programs and terminal prompting. All reviewed `gitutil` paths use the hardened constructor; malicious-config regression tests pass.

11. **[#135 — Escape C1 controls in machine formats](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/135) — clean with advisory.**  
    Adds a bounded, lossless JSON writer that escapes U+0080–U+009F in live output and cache replay paths. The documented limitation is that very old cached payloads containing raw ESC remain outside this specific C1-only replay protection.

12. **[#136 — Confine report and baseline writes](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/136) — changes needed.**  
    The newest commit adds handle-by-handle, identity-verified opening to close a separate symlink TOCTOU race. However, the previously reproduced classification escape remains: [`traversedPath`](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/9a1e6321f0b920f362182638ee6adda9aa7d5685/internal/cli/outputpath.go#L425-L444) skips route inspection whenever there is no `..`. An external alias into a repository subdirectory followed by a repository symlink back outside is classified caller-owned, so execution bypasses the new confined opener and uses plain `os.WriteFile` ([lines 814–826](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/9a1e6321f0b920f362182638ee6adda9aa7d5685/internal/cli/outputpath.go#L814-L826)). The confirmed reproduction overwrote an outside baseline file.

13. **[#137 — Confine `init-agents` writes](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/137) — changes needed.**  
    Adds root-confined reads/writes, link-chain resolution, and filesystem-identity checks. An absolute symlink target is cleaned before kernel traversal validation ([agents.go](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/ae17c6dc349186b180b5492ca2b9855de6801b94/internal/cli/agents.go#L445-L455)). A target shaped like `<repo>/missing/../victim.md` therefore writes `victim.md` even though the raw target is not traversable. This was reproduced and could reach predictable files such as `.git/config`.

14. **[#138 — Confine working-tree reads](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/138) — clean with advisory.**  
    Routes source, prefix, and deferred digest reads through one `os.Root`, preventing `../` and intermediate-symlink escapes. It intentionally refuses even absolute symlinks that point back inside the repository; that compatibility/security tradeoff is documented and tested.

15. **[#139 — Cap every Git blob read](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/139) — clean with advisory.**  
    Applies blob-size ceilings to HEAD reads and both semantic-diff sides, while streaming digest/line metadata for refused blobs so partial failures remain explainable. Memory is bounded, but oversized metadata collection still streams the entire blob, so total I/O/time is not; this is explicitly documented.

16. **[#140 — Bound parser recursion](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/140) — clean with integration caution.**  
    Adds 5,000-level limits across entity extraction, error reporting, Rust unwrapping, parameter patterns, and JS/TS relation walks. Depth failures propagate through completeness and avoid phantom diff changes. This prevents Go stack exhaustion, though C-side tree construction remains primarily bounded by the existing input-size limit.

17. **[#141 — Surface repository ignore exclusions](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/141) — documentation/API changes needed.**  
    Adds provenance-tagged `repo_ignored` reporting, bounded samples, counts, warnings, and partial failures across search formats. The implementation carefully reports lower bounds, but [the documentation](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/778bfd541d887698d016f6bea4289b4a89899215/docs/trust-and-security.md#L94-L102) says counts are exact except for only two cases; Git-listing failure, budget exhaustion, and ignore-byte truncation add further incomplete cases. A public field comment also incorrectly classifies `.git/info/exclude` as repository-controlled.

18. **[#142 — Enforce a wall-clock indexing ceiling](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/142) — contract documentation changes needed.**  
    Adds opt-in `--max-seconds`, cancellation-aware parsing/relations, valid unsafe partial streams, and cache rejection of truncated results. Wall-clock truncation is inherently throughput-dependent, but the repository still promises identical graph output for the same view/options. The same tree and one-second budget produced materially different prefixes under `GOMAXPROCS=1` and `8`. [The new requirements](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/615ba4ab0cc111acdb5caf974f9d2f2f8808d04f/docs/semantic-provider-requirements.md#L367-L373) and byte-identity test claim need to make budget-truncated output an explicit determinism exception.

19. **[#143 — Quarantine forged search records](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/143) — clean with advisory.**  
    Detects source lines resembling tool-authored records such as `VERIFY:`, indents them, adds an untrusted-content notice, and ensures output fitting cannot retain rewritten content after dropping the notice. JSON/NDJSON source bytes remain exact. Documented limits include other commands, presearch, and strong RTL text without explicit bidi controls.

20. **[#144 — Publish re-audited LoCoMo numbers](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/144) — changes needed.**  
    Updates Letta from 80.58 to 84.68 and Supermemory from 77.60 to 82.08, documenting adapter/retry fixes and Supermemory’s effective top-100 cap. The public [README headline](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/f52a9c66c71b0215bf835633440f89e6728e8e57/README.md#L18-L20) still says every arm used 200 items and dates the whole comparison to August 14, contradicting the new August 19–20 runs and effective cap. The run guide also says any zero-context retrieval voids a run, although this PR accepts 114 nonclustered misses, and it still describes seven systems/three fixes instead of eight/four. This docs-only branch contains no raw artifacts, so the scores and miss distribution cannot be independently reproduced from the checkout.

## Merge-order cautions

- #140 and #142 have nine conflict areas; both depth and cancellation guards must survive resolution.
- #141 and #143 conflict in the search text-prefix composition; both disclosure banners are required.
- #130 and #132 overlap substantially in ignore/source listing logic.
- #127, #129, #130, and #141 should receive combined ignore/cache regression tests.
- #138 and #139 should receive a combined `openSource` regression run.

Approval request: may I prepare local fixes for **#97, #128, #130, #131, #132, #136, #137, #141, #142, and #144**, starting with the security-critical #136 and #137? I will not commit, push, comment, or approve anything on GitHub without separate authorization.
Skip 97. Which is the first you want to work on?

Skip #97. My first choice is #136 because it still permits an outside-file overwrite despite the latest confinement rewrite; I’m checking the repository’s current Entire workflow before proposing the exact next move.

Start with **#136**. It’s the highest-risk remaining issue: a path can be misclassified as caller-owned and overwrite a file outside the repository, bypassing the new confined writer entirely.

After #136, I’d do #137, then #132. Approve #136 and I’ll begin with its current head.
Ok, any changes needed on 136?
Yes—there was still a confirmed containment gap at the last reviewed head. Because #136 was actively changing, I’m checking its live head and current trail before stating the exact patch needed.
The latest PR head includes a new fix aimed directly at the containment gap I found. I’m checking that patch and its regression tests now before giving you a yes/no.

Yes. PR #136 still needs one blocking containment fix.

The latest commit fixes aliases between two checkouts, but not this case:

`external alias → repo/subdirectory → repository symlink → outside file`

For paths without `..`, `traversedPath` still skips checking the route, allowing the final write to be treated as caller-owned and performed unconfined. The relevant logic is unchanged from the head where we reproduced the overwrite, and the new tests don’t cover this shape.

Required change: inspect that route even without `..` and add the exact regression test. May I implement it on PR #136?
Yes

I’ll add the exact regression first, make the smallest route-classification fix, and verify it against the PR’s current head. I’m using the repository’s GitHub workflow guidance so the contributor’s branch stays intact; I’ll work on a local branch and won’t publish anything without showing you the verified result.
